name: FAIR Data
title: FAIR Data
answer: FAIR Data is a set of guiding principles for research data and metadata: findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable. It covers datasets, code, models, and documentation across disciplines, not only AI. The aim is to let people and machines discover and use data with clear terms and context. In AI research, FAIR data supports reproducible training, evaluation, and benchmarking.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: FAIR Data is a set of guiding principles for research data and metadata: findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable. It covers datasets, code, models, and documentation across disciplines, not only AI. The aim is to let people and machines discover and use data with clear terms and context. In AI research, FAIR data supports reproducible training, evaluation, and benchmarking.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: FAIR data runs on repositories, persistent identifiers, metadata schemas, controlled vocabularies, and open licenses. Repositories may be domain specific or general, and they assign persistent identifiers such as DOIs. Metadata records describe the data, its creators, methods, and conditions of use. Storage and compute infrastructure support access and processing, but the principles are independent of any single platform.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Researchers create a data management plan, choose a repository, and deposit data with rich metadata. They use standard vocabularies and file formats, and they link data to publications and other outputs. Curation staff review deposits for completeness and compliance. Automated tools can check metadata and generate citations.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: FAIR does not mean open by default, because access can be restricted for privacy, commercial, or ethical reasons. Licenses and data use agreements define what others may do with the data. Provenance records track origin, transformations, and versions, which helps with trust and audit. Sensitive data needs de-identification and controlled access.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: FAIR is increasingly tied to machine-actionable metadata and automated workflows. Funders and journals ask for data availability statements and persistent identifiers. AI models and benchmarks are being published with data cards and model cards. The next steps include better interoperability across repositories and clearer metrics for reuse.
